chunks: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Abu Khalid al-Qammat, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, when two believers meet and shake hands, Allah inserts His Hand between their hands, and shakes the hand of the one who loves his companion more intensely.

key_terms.أَشَدَّهُمَا حُبًّا: The one with more intense love

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of shaking hands between believers in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to emphasize that the physical act of greeting is a conduit for divine presence, where Allah's hand joins the believers'. The specific detail that the one with greater love receives the blessing highlights the spiritual hierarchy of affection (mawaddah) in Shia ethics, encouraging believers to cultivate deep, sincere love for one another as a means of attaining closer proximity to God.
